clauses.reason: The operative lead says: "do order that the said code of fair competition be, and it is hereby, approved, subject to the following conditions". It is a section 3 approval of the Code of Fair Competition for the Motion Picture Industry, so its operative effect was the code's legal force. Under section 3(b) of the Act the approved code's provisions became the standards of fair competition for the trade or industry, under 3(c) the district courts could restrain violations, and under 3(f) a violation was a misdemeanor; that force was the whole operative effect of an approval. The order states no period, condition, 'until' date, stay or provisional approval of its own, and no held record cancels, suspends, modifies under section 10(b) or supersedes the code before June 14, 1935 (see earlier_end_check). Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 (Pub. Res. No. 26, 74th Cong., 49 Stat. 375, approved June 14, 1935) provides: "All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed". The resolution states no effective date other than its approval on June 14, 1935. Repeal of the power to approve codes and of the provisions enforcing them removed the legal force that the approval gave the code, so this clause ended on June 14, 1935; effective date confirmed. The approval is conditional on clauses 1 to 6, which are treated as separate clauses. June 16, 1935, Title I's original two-year expiry, is not an end date: section 1 of the resolution replaced it with April 1, 1936. A. L. A. Schechter Poultry Corp. v. United States, decided May 27, 1935, held the section 3 delegation unconstitutional; it is recorded as a validity characterization (an approval made under an unconstitutional delegation was void from issuance under the doctrine then prevailing), not as an end date, because the decision cancelled no approving order and no held record shows this code cancelled or suspended on May 27, 1935.

Condition 1 says: "the Administrator shall have the right to review, and if necessary, to disapprove any act taken by the code authority, or by any committee named by it, and any act taken by any board named by it". It is a reserved power over the code authority created by the code; it has no object once the code and its code authority lose legal force. It is code-dependent, states no period, and no held record ends it early. It is a command under the section 3 approval of the Motion Picture Industry code, so its force was the code's. research_rationale:
EO 6458 (1933-11-27, Franklin D. Roosevelt), read in full in the held American Presidency Project transcription (registered grade mirror_transcription, not an original; 3808 characters). Identity: the census register lists it as 'Executive Order 6458—Code of Fair Competition for the Motion Picture Industry' dated 1933-11-27; the WPA 1944 list has '1933 Nov 27 p.552: Code of Fair Competition for the Motion Picture Indus try approved. III NRA Codes 215.'. Page check: the mirror page record with the same source sha256 is headed 'Executive Order 6458—Code of Fair Competition for the Motion Picture Industry', dated 1933-11-27, from a common-crawl capture of 2024-11-02T18:47:33Z, and its text_sha256 equals the held text's; the heading names this order's number and the date and subject agree with the text. Machine inventory checked and kept: the operative lead (approval) and six numbered conditions. Operative lead: the President orders "that the said code of fair competition be, and it is hereby, approved, subject to the following conditions": the Code of Fair Competition for the Motion Picture Industry (title I, section 3(a)). Conditions 1 to 3 give the Administrator powers over the code authority; 4 and 6 suspend code provisions pending a further report from the Administrator; 5 provides that certain code provisions do not take effect for writers, authors and dramatists. Each is a command that depends on the approved code. First end of every clause: S.J. Res. 113 section 2, June 14, 1935; no earlier end is held (see clause reasons and earlier_end_check).

savings.reason: Acts done under the approved code before June 14, 1935, and any liability for violating it before that date, are accrued effects. The general savings statute of the time (not a held source) preserved liabilities already incurred under a repealed statute; that preservation does not keep the approval operative. Section 5 of the Act exempted from the antitrust laws "any code, agreement, or license approved, prescribed, or issued and in effect under this title" and complying action while Title I was in effect and for sixty days after; whatever exemption survives for action taken before the repeal is an accrued effect. The proviso in section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 says the exemption "shall extend only to agreements and action thereunder" of two kinds (section 7(a) requirements, and prohibiting practices already unlawful); it names agreements, not codes, and states no time limit, so the held text does not settle whether it narrowed the exemption for action taken under codes before June 14, 1935. No held source continues this approval after June 14, 1935 and no held source shows a prosecution continued after that date.
